properties.description: Framework paper with author-narrated case studies in medical imaging, computer vision, particle physics, causal diagnosis and meteor detection. No measured evaluation of the framework.
MLTRL: ten readiness levels with gated reviews, TRL Cards, risk quantification and switchbacks for developing and deploying ML systems.

properties.population: ML teams and stakeholders in any domain; healthcare is one example
properties.decision: whether a ML technology has matured enough to advance a level

relation_assertions.rationale: A reusable governance, audit and reporting framework; it contains no model, so only the component profile fits and no world-model capability is claimed.
Reviewer mapping only: governance, reporting and monitoring practices could inform a safety and runtime-assurance module. No healthcare world model or evidence is involved.
Reviewer mapping only: lifecycle and release governance practice; the paper does not mention clinicians or healthcare world models as its own scope.

capability_assessments.rationale: A process framework for ML development. It specifies no state, transition, action or prediction model, so the identity rule cannot be met. Case-study systems are cited and their capabilities are not inherited.

gate_assessments.rationale: No state-transition prediction exists in a process framework.
The framework prescribes risk quantification, monitoring and review, but no fail behavior is specified or tested for any healthcare system.
Governance, change control and monitoring are prescribed at process level; templates are promised and not provided, and no deployment is documented.

This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Included only as supporting reusable ML readiness/audit and reporting framework; it is not a healthcare world model and provides no demonstrated healthcare state-transition model. Figure 4 text is garbled in the extraction (PDF p. 10), but it is unrelated to the extracted fields; no relevant table was unreadable. A:I were left untouched. Evidence QA: 4/5 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (80%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 5 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Full bibliography entries on pages 22–26 were subsequently read in the targeted 2026-11-22 local review; cited full studies remain unretrieved. Case-study results (neuropathology, recycling, Etalumis, causal diagnosis, CAMS) are cited work and are not inherited as capabilities of MLTRL or of any world model.

The framework is not healthcare-specific and has no world-model content. Feature assertions are at the level of the framework's own process requirements and its recommendations, kept at claim or specification stage. They show what the framework asks for, not that a system satisfies it.

No measured evaluation of MLTRL's benefits is reported, so the author statement that it is proven rests on narrated examples. The TRL Card templates are promised at publication and were not available.
